Full story by Alejandro Serrano at Texas Tribune: texastribune.org/2026/05/13/…

More on immigration politics and enforcement data: austinkocher.substack.com

This is worth watching carefully heading into the Nov midterms. Immigration as a Republican asset depended on a specific grievance,chaotic border crossings, that has largely resolved. Whether interior enforcement generates the same political energy is an open empirical question.

The shift reflects a real policy change: illegal border crossings are down sharply. But the issue has moved from the border to the interior, deportations of people with no criminal record, deaths of U.S. citizens in enforcement operations, and a party divided on what comes next.

In April 2024, 68% of Texas Republican voters called immigration or border security the state's most important problem, the highest in recent memory. New polling from the UT Texas Politics Project shows it has now fallen to its lowest priority level in recent history.

Full story by Camilo Montoya-Galvez at CBS News: cbsnews.com/news/trump-guant…

More on detention data and what the numbers actually show: austinkocher.substack.com

The legality is still being litigated. A federal judge in D.C. found in December that the operation was likely unlawful, but didn't block it. The gap between announced scale and operational reality is one of the clearest data points we have on distance between rhetoric and fact.

the DoD operation is projected at $73 million, per figures provided to Sen. Elizabeth Warren, up from a previously reported $40M estimate. Over the past year, 832 detainees have passed through on 100+ flights. This week, government staff outnumbered detainees roughly 100 to 1.
Trump promised 30,000 immigration detainees at Guantanamo Bay. As of May 11, the U.S. was holding 6. Capacity at the facility is 400 beds. Fewer than 2% were occupied.

Weird way to remind people that, amid native born decline in birth rate and huge aging population, immigrants are hard working members of society who deserve legal pathways into our workforce so we can stay competitive in the global economy.


Center for Immigration Studies (@CIS_org)

Millions came illegally.

Many of them realized they could get work permits if they simply applied for asylum.

Now they aren’t coming to court because they never wanted asylum — they wanted to work.

cis.org/Arth

Full story: nytimes.com/2026/05/13/us/po…

More on the infrastructure of immigration enforcement: austinkocher.substack.com

Undocumented immigrants paid an estimated $96.7 billion in federal, state, and local taxes in 2022, per the Institute on Taxation and Economic Policy. If ITIN access narrows, the government likely collects less revenue, not more.
A prior IRS-ICE data-sharing agreement, designed to give ICE access to home addresses has already been blocked in court. The ITIN change would work differently, restructuring who can obtain the code.

The Trump admin is now discussing changes to the ITIN (the 9-digit tax ID that undocumented immigrants use to file taxes) that could force people to disclose immigration status or disengage from the tax system entirely.

Read. It. 

- no pathway to citizenship
- fines for people who broke the law
- America-first principles throughout

I'm not really for or against this bill, but JFC, if you're on the right and you don't like this, you really aren't interested in solving actual problems.
The Dignity Act isn't perfect but watching Nativists parrot "amnesty" is an embarrassing admission that they haven't read it and don't understand it. #amnestyparrots

Full story by Alex Nguyen at Texas Tribune: texastribune.org/2026/05/13/…

More on how 287(g) data fits the broader enforcement picture: austinkocher.substack.com
The question the data raises: if Dallas County is already producing thousands of ICE detainers, what is the 287(g) requirement actually adding, enforcement capacity, or political accountability?
Texas sheriffs have now signed 270+ 287(g) agreements as of May 12, per ICE data but Dallas County's detainer volume already put it in the national top 10 without one.

Dallas County Jail logged more than 4,000 ICE detainers between Sept. 2023 and July 2025, without a formal 287(g) agreement. Now AG Paxton is threatening Sheriff Marian Brown for not signing one, even though her legal deadline is Dec. 1.
